texto.titulo: Thermal and energy effects of extensive green roofs on low-rise office buildings in a hot semi-arid city
texto.autores: M. Arvelo, K. Thornquist and S. Mabuza-Reyes
texto.abstract: Extensive green roofs are increasingly promoted as a means of mitigating the thermal loads imposed on buildings in hot cities, yet field evidence from semi-arid climates remains scarce and is largely confined to short monitoring campaigns on single buildings. This study examined the extent to which extensive green roofs reduce roof surface temperature, top-floor air temperature and cooling energy consumption in low-rise office buildings in Valdoro, a hot semi-arid city. Twelve buildings with green roofs were paired with twelve comparable buildings with conventional roofs and monitored over a 122-day hot season, with cooling electricity sub-metered at 15-minute intervals. Green roofs lowered the mean daily peak roof surface temperature by 27.6 °C and seasonal cooling electricity by 18.8% per unit floor area, although the savings were concentrated on the uppermost storey and declined sharply on non-irrigated roofs during a prolonged heatwave. It is concluded that the benefits of green roofs in such climates are real but conditional, depending on substrate depth, moisture availability and the thermal characteristics of the roof beneath.
texto.keywords: green roofs, cooling energy, roof surface temperature, semi-arid climate, evapotranspiration, urban adaptation

blocos.p: Cities in hot climates face a compounding problem. Rising mean temperatures and more frequent heatwaves increase the thermal loads imposed on buildings, while the cooling systems installed in response consume electricity at precisely the hours when grids are most strained and, where that electricity is generated from fossil fuels, release the emissions that contribute to further warming. Roofs occupy a disproportionate place in this problem. In low-rise districts they may account for between a fifth and a quarter of the exposed urban surface, and because they receive solar radiation almost uninterrupted from mid-morning to late afternoon, conventional roof membranes routinely reach temperatures far above that of the surrounding air. It is therefore unsurprising that interventions at roof level, among which green roofs have attracted particular attention, have come to occupy a central place in municipal climate adaptation plans.

A green roof consists, in its extensive form, of a thin growing medium, typically between 5 and 20 cm deep, planted with drought-tolerant vegetation and laid over drainage and root-barrier layers on top of the waterproofing membrane. Several mechanisms have been proposed to explain how such a system moderates the temperature of the roof beneath it, including the shading of the substrate by foliage and the additional thermal mass of the saturated medium. Broadly, however, two accounts of the cooling effect may be distinguished in the literature: one which attributes it principally to the passive insulating properties of the substrate and drainage layers, and another which attributes it principally to the latent heat consumed by evapotranspiration from plants and moist soil. The first account implies that the benefit should be relatively stable over time, provided that the layers remain intact, whereas the second implies that the benefit fluctuates with the availability of water and may all but disappear when the substrate dries out. It is the latter that is most directly put to the test in hot semi-arid climates, where rainfall during the hot season is negligible and irrigation is costly.

Much of the empirical evidence on these effects has been produced in temperate climates. Marlowe and Achterberg (2012), monitoring six paired roofs over two summers, reported reductions in peak membrane temperature of up to 20 °C and suggested that the size of the benefit increases roughly in proportion to the solar radiation incident on the roof. Comparable reductions in surface temperature were subsequently documented in a number of field studies, although their translation into energy savings has proved less straightforward. Ostrowska (2018), drawing on the metered consumption of fourteen office buildings, estimated whole-building cooling savings of only 6 to 9%, a figure she attributed to the modest cooling demand of temperate summers rather than to any shortcoming of the roofs themselves. Rastogi (2016) had earlier argued, on the basis of storey-by-storey simulations, that the savings achieved by green roofs are concentrated almost entirely in the uppermost storey, so that whole-building figures will tend to decline as the number of storeys increases.

Studies conducted in hot climates have, for the most part, relied on simulation. Quispe-Delgado (2015), modelling a two-storey office building under the climatic conditions of several arid cities, predicted cooling energy savings of up to 25%, considerably more than those observed in temperate settings. Such estimates have been received with some caution. Halloran et al. (2017) pointed out that most simulation tools assume a substrate kept permanently at or near field capacity, an assumption which is seldom satisfied on unirrigated roofs in dry climates, and they argued that predicted savings are accordingly likely to be overstated. Field evidence from hot-humid cities, where moisture is less limiting, offers partial support for the higher estimates: Nwachukwu and Brandt (2019) recorded top-floor air temperatures 2.3 °C lower beneath a green roof than beneath an adjacent conventional roof over a three-week monitoring campaign. Whether results of this kind may be extended to semi-arid conditions, in which the hot season coincides with the dry season, remains an open question.

The methodological limitations of the existing field studies have also been noted. Ferreira-Lunde (2020), in a review of 41 monitoring studies, found that fewer than a third had lasted longer than one month and that most had compared a single green roof with a single reference roof, so that differences between the two buildings could not be separated from the effect of the roof itself. Takemura and Ilesanmi (2021) drew attention to a further confounding factor, namely the thermal resistance of the roof assembly beneath the vegetation. In their sample of retrofitted schools, buildings whose roof slabs had already been insulated to current standards gained little from the addition of a vegetated layer, since most of the heat it intercepted would in any case have been blocked by the insulation below; for poorly insulated buildings, by contrast, they reported reductions in cooling demand nearly three times as large. Vandersloot et al. (2022), finally, cautioned that in water-scarce cities any energy saving must be weighed against the water consumed in keeping the vegetation alive, a trade-off which they considered to have been largely neglected.

Taken together, these studies suggest that the thermal benefit of green roofs is well established at the level of the roof surface, whereas the extent to which it translates into reduced cooling energy consumption in occupied buildings is considerably less certain, particularly in climates where water is scarce during the hottest months. Field studies that monitor a sufficiently large number of buildings over an entire hot season, that compare green and conventional roofs on otherwise similar buildings and that measure cooling energy directly rather than inferring it from surface temperatures remain, to the authors' knowledge, rare in semi-arid cities. The present study was designed to address this gap. Its purpose was not to establish whether green roofs are cooler than conventional roofs, which few would now dispute, but to estimate how much of that difference reaches the occupied spaces and the electricity meter, and under what conditions.

The study sought to quantify the thermal and energy effects of extensive green roofs on low-rise office buildings in a hot semi-arid city over a complete hot season. Four research questions were formulated: (1) To what extent do daily peak roof surface temperatures differ between buildings with green roofs and buildings with conventional roofs? (2) Is the air temperature of the uppermost occupied storey lower beneath green roofs than beneath conventional roofs? (3) How much electricity per unit floor area is consumed for cooling in each group, and how is any difference distributed between the uppermost and the lower storeys? (4) Are the effects identified in questions 1 to 3 moderated by the depth of the growing medium and by the irrigation regime? It was hypothesised, on the basis of the literature reviewed above, that green roofs would reduce cooling consumption to a greater degree than has been reported in temperate climates, but that this reduction would be smaller on non-irrigated roofs.

Valdoro is a city of approximately 1.4 million inhabitants situated on an inland plateau at an elevation of 640 m. Its climate is classified as hot semi-arid: mean daily maximum temperatures exceed 36 °C from June to September, peaking at 38.6 °C in July, and fewer than 15 mm of the annual rainfall of 310 mm falls during these four months. Electricity demand for air conditioning has been estimated to account for nearly half of the city's summer peak load. In 2019 the municipality introduced an ordinance offering a reduction in property tax to owners of commercial buildings who installed vegetated roofs, and by the end of 2023 some 210 such roofs had been registered, the great majority of them on office buildings of two to four storeys in the central and northern districts.

A paired comparative design was adopted. Candidate buildings were drawn from the municipal registry and from the cadastral records of the same districts, and were considered eligible if they were office buildings of two to four storeys, had been constructed between 1995 and 2012, had a flat roof of between 400 and 1,200 m², were cooled by a central variable refrigerant flow system and had a roof slab with a thermal transmittance (U-value) of between 0.9 and 1.3 W/m²K. Of the 63 green-roof buildings meeting these criteria, 12 were selected for which a conventional-roof counterpart could be found within 1.5 km that matched them in number of storeys, in floor area to within 15% and in principal façade orientation. The resulting sample therefore comprised 24 buildings arranged in 12 pairs. All of the green roofs were of the extensive type and had been installed at least two years before the study began, so that the vegetation could be considered established; six had a growing medium 8 cm deep and six a medium 15 cm deep, and seven were drip-irrigated while five relied on rainfall alone. The conventional roofs were finished either with a light grey bituminous membrane (n = 8) or with exposed concrete (n = 4).

Measurements were taken over the 122 days from 1 June to 30 September 2024, following a two-week period in May during which all instruments were installed, checked against a reference sensor and adjusted where necessary. Roof surface temperature was recorded at 10-minute intervals by type-T thermocouples fixed to the outer face of the waterproofing membrane at three locations on each roof; on the green roofs, the sensors were therefore located beneath the growing medium and drainage layer, at the point where heat enters the roof slab. These measurements were complemented by infrared thermographic surveys carried out every fortnight at 14:00 and by soil moisture probes installed on four of the green roofs. Indoor air temperature was recorded on the uppermost storey only, by three shielded data loggers per building mounted at a height of 1.1 m in occupied offices away from windows and supply diffusers. Electricity consumed by the cooling system was sub-metered separately for each storey at 15-minute intervals, and outdoor conditions were obtained from a weather station installed on the roof of one conventional building near the centre of the study area.

Daily peak values were extracted from the surface and indoor temperature series, and cooling electricity was summed by day and normalised by conditioned floor area. Differences between the two groups were estimated by linear mixed-effects models in which roof type was entered as a fixed effect and building pair as a random effect, with daily cooling degree-days and the proportion of occupied workstations, obtained from the buildings' access-control logs, included as covariates. The moderating effects of substrate depth and irrigation were examined within the green-roof group only, given that the sample was too small to support a full factorial analysis. A heatwave was defined as a period of at least three consecutive days on which the outdoor maximum exceeded 42 °C; one such event, lasting from 12 to 19 August, occurred during the study and was analysed separately. Records affected by sensor or meter failures, amounting to 3.4% of the total, were excluded, and a significance level of 0.05 was adopted throughout.

Over the study period as a whole, the mean daily peak membrane temperature was 61.4 °C (SD = 4.2) on the conventional roofs and 33.8 °C (SD = 3.1) on the green roofs, a difference of 27.6 °C (95% CI 25.9–29.3; p < 0.001). The highest single value, 74.2 °C, was recorded on an exposed concrete roof on 15 August, during the heatwave, when the membrane beneath the nearest green roof did not exceed 41.0 °C. Differences of this magnitude were observed in all twelve pairs, though with considerable variation between them, the smallest pair difference being 19.8 °C and the largest 34.5 °C. Night-time minima, by contrast, differed little between the groups (22.6 °C and 24.1 °C for conventional and green roofs respectively), so that the green roofs exhibited a consistently pronounced attenuation of the diurnal temperature range, which averaged 9.7 °C beneath the growing medium against 38.8 °C on the conventional membranes.

Within the green-roof group, both substrate depth and irrigation were associated with lower membrane temperatures, though the two moderators behaved quite differently over the season. Roofs with a 15 cm growing medium had a mean daily peak of 31.9 °C, compared with 35.7 °C for those with an 8 cm medium (difference 3.8 °C; p = 0.02), and this difference remained broadly constant from June to September. The effect of irrigation, on the other hand, was negligible for most of the season: outside the heatwave, irrigated and non-irrigated roofs differed by only 1.6 °C (p = 0.21). During the heatwave, however, the mean daily peak beneath the non-irrigated roofs rose to 44.9 °C, whereas that beneath the irrigated roofs rose only to 34.1 °C, a difference of 10.8 °C (p < 0.001). The soil moisture probes indicated that the volumetric water content of the non-irrigated media had fallen below 8% by the third day of the event.

Indoor air temperatures on the uppermost storey were lower beneath the green roofs throughout the season. During occupied hours (08:00–18:00), the mean air temperature was 25.0 °C in the green-roof buildings and 26.9 °C in the conventional buildings, a difference of 1.9 °C (p < 0.001). This difference should be interpreted in light of the fact that all buildings were air-conditioned to set-points of between 23 and 25 °C, so that it reflects not the free-running thermal response of the storey but the extent to which the cooling systems failed to hold the set-point during the afternoon. On this measure the contrast was striking: the proportion of occupied hours in which the top-floor temperature exceeded 27 °C was 23.5% in the conventional buildings but only 6.8% in the green-roof buildings.

Seasonal cooling electricity consumption averaged 26.6 kWh/m² in the conventional buildings and 21.6 kWh/m² in the green-roof buildings, a reduction of 18.8% (p = 0.004) after adjustment for cooling degree-days and occupancy. As anticipated by the third research question, however, this reduction was far from evenly distributed between storeys. On the uppermost storey, consumption was 31.2% lower in the green-roof buildings, whereas on the storeys below the difference was only 3.1% and did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.27). Peak cooling demand, defined as the highest 15-minute load recorded in each building, was on average 14.5% lower in the green-roof group.

Table 1 summarises the seasonal cooling savings by roof configuration, each green-roof building being compared with its conventional pair. The largest savings were obtained on deep irrigated roofs (n = 4; 24.9%), followed by deep non-irrigated (n = 2; 19.4%), shallow irrigated (n = 3; 17.2%) and shallow non-irrigated roofs (n = 3; 11.6%). The table also reports savings for the heatwave week alone, and it is here that the configurations diverged most sharply: whereas irrigated roofs maintained savings of 22.3% (deep) and 16.0% (shallow) during the event, the savings of non-irrigated roofs fell to 9.1% and 4.1% respectively. In other words, the shallow non-irrigated roofs, which make up the most common configuration in the municipal registry, delivered less than a fifth of the saving of the best configuration at precisely the time when cooling demand was highest.

The first research question can be answered unambiguously. The reduction in peak membrane temperature observed here, at 27.6 °C, is considerably larger than the reductions of up to 20 °C reported by Marlowe and Achterberg (2012) for temperate summers, a result which is consistent with their suggestion that the benefit increases with incident solar radiation. It should be borne in mind, however, that the sensors in the present study were fixed to the membrane beneath the growing medium, whereas several earlier studies measured the temperature of the vegetated surface itself; since the latter is exposed to the sun and the former is not, figures obtained by the two methods are not strictly comparable, and the difference between them is likely to account for some part of the discrepancy. More significant, perhaps, is the finding that the night-time minima of the two groups were similar, which suggests that the green roofs did not store heat during the day to release it into the building at night, as has occasionally been feared.

The answers to the second and third research questions are more nuanced. Green roofs lowered the cooling electricity consumed by the buildings by almost a fifth, a saving well above the 6 to 9% reported by Ostrowska (2018) for temperate office buildings, yet below the 25% predicted by Quispe-Delgado (2015) for arid climates. Crucially, the saving was confined almost entirely to the uppermost storey, that is, to the zone separated from the green roof by nothing more than the roof slab and a suspended ceiling. This pattern lends empirical support to the argument advanced by Rastogi (2016) and implies that whole-building savings in Valdoro would have been smaller had the sample included taller buildings: assuming equal consumption on each storey, a saving of 31.2% on the top storey and of 3.1% on the remainder would amount to little more than 10% in a four-storey building. It follows that the frequently cited percentage savings for green roofs are, in the absence of information on building height, of limited value for policy.

The fourth research question bears most directly on the two accounts of the cooling effect outlined in the introduction. Had the benefit of the green roofs derived principally from the insulating properties of their layers, it should have been largely unaffected by the drying of the substrate. In fact, the non-irrigated roofs lost much of their advantage during the heatwave, whereas substrate depth, which governs both the insulating capacity and the water-holding capacity of the medium, conferred a stable benefit throughout the season. This pattern is most plausibly explained by an evapotranspirative effect that is substantial while moisture is available and that collapses once the water held in the medium has been exhausted, as Halloran et al. (2017) had anticipated. Non-irrigated roofs nonetheless continued to outperform the conventional roofs throughout the event, albeit by a much narrower margin, which suggests that the passive insulating effect, though secondary, is far from negligible. Neither account, then, is sufficient on its own.

These findings carry several implications for the municipal programme. Since the benefit was concentrated beneath the roof, and since Takemura and Ilesanmi (2021) found that it is largely pre-empted where the slab is already well insulated, incentives would be better directed towards poorly insulated low-rise buildings than distributed uniformly across the commercial stock. Deeper growing media appear to offer a benefit which does not depend on water, though at the cost of greater structural loads, which not all existing roofs may be able to bear. Irrigation, by contrast, delivered its benefit precisely when it was most needed, but at a cost in water that, as Vandersloot et al. (2022) have warned, cannot be taken for granted in a water-scarce city. Drip irrigation using treated greywater from the buildings themselves may offer a way out of this dilemma, provided that its quality can be assured and that the volumes involved prove to be modest; the present study, however, did not measure water consumption and can offer no estimate of those volumes.

Several limitations should be acknowledged. First, the study covered a single hot season in a single city, and the results may not hold in years with longer or more intense heatwaves, nor in semi-arid cities with different building traditions. Second, although twelve pairs represent a larger sample than most previous field studies, the number of buildings in each green-roof configuration was small, and the comparisons reported in Table 1 should accordingly be regarded as indicative rather than conclusive. Third, the buildings were not randomly assigned to roof types: the owners who chose to install green roofs might differ systematically from those who did not, for instance in the attention they pay to the maintenance of their cooling systems, and although occupancy was controlled for, differences of this kind cannot be ruled out. Finally, only office buildings with similar roof insulation were included, which, while it strengthened the internal validity of the comparison, means that the moderating role of insulation identified by Takemura and Ilesanmi (2021) could not be examined.

Future research might address these limitations in several ways. Monitoring the same buildings over several consecutive years would make it possible to determine whether the benefits persist as the vegetation matures or, conversely, decline as substrates compact and drainage layers clog. Studies that include residential and taller buildings, as well as buildings with a wider range of roof insulation levels, are needed before the findings can be generalised to the urban stock as a whole. The water consumed by irrigation should be metered directly, so that the energy and water balances of each configuration can be compared, and life-cycle assessments could also establish whether the savings reported here justify the costs of installation and maintenance over the service life of the roof. Lastly, the present study was confined to the building scale; whether the green roofs of Valdoro have any measurable effect on air temperatures at street level remains to be investigated.

This study has shown that, in a hot semi-arid city, extensive green roofs lowered the mean daily peak temperature of the roof membrane by almost 28 °C, kept the uppermost storey of air-conditioned office buildings nearly 2 °C cooler during working hours and reduced seasonal cooling electricity by close to a fifth. These benefits, however, were neither uniform nor unconditional. They were concentrated on the top storey, they were larger on deeper growing media, and on roofs without irrigation they diminished markedly during the very period of extreme heat in which they would have been most valuable.

It is concluded that green roofs should be regarded not as a universal remedy for the thermal problems of buildings in hot cities, but as a targeted measure whose value depends on the building beneath and on the water available above. Where water cannot be supplied during the hottest weeks, the evaporative component of the benefit will be lost, whatever the merits of the planting scheme; where the roof slab is already well insulated, much of the remaining benefit will already have been secured by other means. Municipal programmes such as that of Valdoro would therefore achieve more by concentrating incentives on poorly insulated low-rise buildings, by favouring deeper growing media where structures permit, and by linking support for green roofs to a sustainable source of irrigation water, than by rewarding the installation of vegetated roofs as such.

questoes.enunciado: Com base no título e no resumo, o tema do estudo reportado no texto é
alternativas: os benefícios ambientais dos telhados verdes no combate às ilhas de calor urbanas em cidades de diferentes climas.
o papel da irrigação no desempenho térmico de telhados verdes durante ondas de calor prolongadas.

o efeito de telhados verdes extensivos sobre a temperatura da superfície da cobertura, a temperatura do ar no último pavimento e o consumo de energia para refrigeração em edifícios baixos de escritórios de uma cidade de clima quente semiárido.
a influência de telhados verdes extensivos sobre a temperatura do ar externo e a demanda de energia para aquecimento em edifícios comerciais de uma cidade semiárida.
as dificuldades de implantação de telhados verdes em edifícios de escritórios, considerando os custos de irrigação em cidades com escassez de água.
questoes.explicacao:
O resumo diz: This study examined the extent to which extensive green roofs reduce roof surface temperature, top-floor air temperature and cooling energy consumption in low-rise office buildings in Valdoro, a hot semi-arid city. A alternativa (c) reproduz as três variáveis (superfície, último pavimento, refrigeração) e o recorte (edifícios baixos de escritórios, cidade quente semiárida).

(a) é ampla demais: o estudo não trata de ilhas de calor nem de “diferentes climas”, e o próprio texto diz, no §22, que o efeito na temperatura do ar da rua não foi investigado. (b) é estreita demais: a irrigação é só um dos moderadores (pergunta 4). (d) troca as palavras: não é temperatura do ar externo nem aquecimento (heating), e sim superfície da cobertura e refrigeração (cooling). (e) fala de “dificuldades” e custos, que o estudo não mediu (custos aparecem só como pesquisa futura, §22).
questoes.dica: Dica: o tema está no título + na frase do resumo que diz o que o estudo examinou (This study examined…). Descarte o que é mais amplo (outro assunto, “diferentes climas”), o que é mais estreito (uma única variável ou moderador) e o que troca uma palavra-chave (aquecimento × refrigeração, ar externo × superfície, dificuldades × efeitos).

questoes.enunciado: No segmento “It is the latter that is most directly put to the test in hot semi-arid climates” (§2), o segmento destacado refere-se a
alternativas: “one which attributes it principally to the passive insulating properties of the substrate and drainage layers” (§2).
“the additional thermal mass of the saturated medium” (§2).
“the shading of the substrate by foliage” (§2).
“the benefit should be relatively stable over time, provided that the layers remain intact” (§2).
“another which attributes it principally to the latent heat consumed by evapotranspiration from plants and moist soil” (§2).
questoes.explicacao:
The latter (“este último”, “o segundo de dois”) só pode apontar para um par. O par está em two accounts of the cooling effect may be distinguished: one which … and another which …. A frase seguinte continua a comparar os dois (The first account … whereas the second …), e the latter retoma o segundo: a explicação pela evapotranspiração. Faz sentido: é essa explicação que fica “posta à prova” onde não chove no verão e irrigar é caro.

(a) é the former (o primeiro). (b) e (c) são mecanismos citados antes, mas não fazem parte do par de accounts. (d) é a consequência do primeiro relato, não do segundo.
questoes.dica: Dica: the former = o primeiro e the latter = o último de dois itens. Procure no texto anterior uma estrutura de par (one … another, X and Y, the first … the second), mesmo que esteja algumas frases antes. Depois, confirme pelo sentido da frase.

questoes.enunciado:
Nos parágrafos 3 a 5, os autores apresentam achados e argumentos de estudos anteriores. Associe as colunas, relacionando cada afirmação a seu(s) respectivo(s) autor(es).

  1. Marlowe and Achterberg (2012)
  2. Ostrowska (2018)
  3. Rastogi (2016)
  4. Halloran et al. (2017)
  5. Ferreira-Lunde (2020)
  • (  )As economias se concentram quase inteiramente no último pavimento, de modo que os números do edifício inteiro tendem a cair à medida que aumenta o número de pavimentos.
  • (  )A maioria das ferramentas de simulação supõe um substrato mantido permanentemente úmido, o que tende a superestimar as economias previstas.
  • (  )O baixo percentual de economia observado se deve à pequena demanda de refrigeração dos verões temperados, e não a deficiências dos telhados.
  • (  )Poucos estudos de monitoramento duraram mais de um mês, e a maioria comparou um único telhado verde com um único telhado de referência.
  • (  )O tamanho do benefício cresce aproximadamente em proporção à radiação solar incidente sobre a cobertura.

Assinale a sequência correta.
questoes.explicacao:
the savings achieved by green roofs are concentrated almost entirely in the uppermost storey, so that whole-building figures will tend to decline… → Rastogi (3), §3.

most simulation tools assume a substrate kept permanently at or near field capacity … predicted savings are accordingly likely to be overstated → Halloran et al. (4), §4.

a figure she attributed to the modest cooling demand of temperate summers rather than to any shortcoming of the roofs themselves → Ostrowska (2), §3.

fewer than a third had lasted longer than one month and … most had compared a single green roof with a single reference roof → Ferreira-Lunde (5), §5.

the size of the benefit increases roughly in proportion to the solar radiation incident on the roof → Marlowe and Achterberg (1), §3.
questoes.dica: Dica: ache o nome de cada autor no texto e leia a frase inteira em que ele aparece, inclusive o que vem depois de vírgula (a figure she attributed to…). Quando dois autores estão no mesmo parágrafo, como Ostrowska e Rastogi no §3, a troca entre eles é a armadilha mais comum.

questoes.enunciado: Os segmentos destacados em “In their sample of retrofitted schools, buildings whose roof slabs had already been insulated to current standards gained little from the addition of a vegetated layer, since most of the heat it intercepted would in any case have been blocked by the insulation below; for poorly insulated buildings, by contrast, they reported reductions in cooling demand nearly three times as large” (§5) referem-se, respectivamente, a
alternativas: Ferreira-Lunde – buildings – roof slab – poorly insulated buildings
Takemura and Ilesanmi – roof slabs – vegetated layer – poorly insulated buildings
Takemura and Ilesanmi – buildings – insulation – Takemura and Ilesanmi
Takemura and Ilesanmi – buildings – vegetated layer – Takemura and Ilesanmi
retrofitted schools – buildings – vegetated layer – poorly insulated buildings
questoes.explicacao:
their: a frase anterior fala de Takemura and Ilesanmi (2021) drew attention to…. A amostra de escolas é deles. Ferreira-Lunde é singular e está em outra frase.

whose: o pronome relativo retoma o substantivo imediatamente anterior, buildings: “edifícios cujas lajes…”. Não pode ser roof slabs, que é justamente o que vem depois dele (a coisa possuída).

it: singular. Quem “intercepta” o calor antes de ele chegar ao isolamento “abaixo” (below) é a camada vegetada (a vegetated layer). Insulation é o que bloquearia o calor, não o que o intercepta.

they: plural. Poorly insulated buildings está logo antes e é a armadilha, mas edifícios não “relatam” (reported) reduções. Quem relata são os autores do estudo, Takemura e Ilesanmi.
questoes.dica: Método: (1) singular ou plural (it × they/their); (2) liste os candidatos compatíveis, inclusive os da frase anterior; (3) teste o sentido com o verbo (they reported: só pessoas relatam). O candidato mais próximo nem sempre é o certo. Em whose, o referente é o substantivo que vem antes, e o que vem depois é o que lhe pertence.

questoes.enunciado: Assinale a alternativa que NÃO faz parte das perguntas de pesquisa do estudo (§7).
alternativas: Os efeitos dos telhados verdes são moderados pelo nível de isolamento térmico da laje de cobertura?
Em que medida as temperaturas máximas diárias da superfície da cobertura diferem entre edifícios com telhados verdes e com telhados convencionais?
A temperatura do ar no último pavimento ocupado é menor sob telhados verdes do que sob telhados convencionais?
Quanta eletricidade por unidade de área é consumida para refrigeração em cada grupo, e como a diferença se distribui entre o último pavimento e os inferiores?
Os efeitos observados são moderados pela profundidade do substrato e pelo regime de irrigação?
questoes.explicacao:
As quatro perguntas do §7 correspondem a (b) (1) To what extent do daily peak roof surface temperatures differ…, (c) (2) Is the air temperature of the uppermost occupied storey lower…, (d) (3) How much electricity per unit floor area is consumed for cooling… e (e) (4) … moderated by the depth of the growing medium and by the irrigation regime.

(a) é o intruso. O papel do isolamento vem de Takemura e Ilesanmi (§5), e os autores controlaram esse fator, escolhendo edifícios com U-value semelhante (§9). Por isso, no §21, dizem que the moderating role of insulation … could not be examined.
questoes.dica: Dica: em “NÃO faz parte”, ache a lista (aqui numerada de 1 a 4) e marque cada alternativa com o número correspondente. O intruso costuma ser um tema do próprio texto, tirado da revisão de literatura ou das limitações, por isso parece plausível.

questoes.enunciado:
Sobre o método do estudo, indique se os segmentos a seguir estão em acordo (A) ou desacordo (D) com o que apresentam os parágrafos 9 e 10.

  • (  )Os 24 edifícios da amostra foram escolhidos entre os 63 que atendiam aos critérios de elegibilidade.
  • (  )Cada edifício com telhado verde foi pareado com um edifício de cobertura convencional situado a até 1,5 km, com o mesmo número de pavimentos e área de piso com diferença máxima de 15%.
  • (  )Todos os telhados verdes eram do tipo extensivo, e a maioria deles era irrigada por gotejamento.
  • (  )As medições estenderam-se por 122 dias, de junho a setembro de 2024, e a temperatura do ar interno foi registrada em todos os pavimentos dos edifícios.

Assinale a sequência correta.
alternativas: A – A – A – D
D – A – D – D
A – D – A – A
D – A – A – D
D – D – A – D
questoes.explicacao:
1 (D): Of the 63 green-roof buildings meeting these criteria, 12 were selected. Os 63 são só os edifícios com telhado verde, e deles saíram 12. Os 12 convencionais foram buscados depois, como pares.

2 (A): a conventional-roof counterpart could be found within 1.5 km that matched them in number of storeys, in floor area to within 15% and in principal façade orientation.

3 (A): All of the green roofs were of the extensive type e seven were drip-irrigated while five relied on rainfall alone. Sete de doze é a maioria.

4 (D): o período está certo (122 days from 1 June to 30 September 2024), mas Indoor air temperature was recorded on the uppermost storey only. Quem foi medido por pavimento foi a eletricidade (sub-metered separately for each storey).
questoes.dica: Dica: nos itens sobre método, confira número por número e veja a que cada número se refere (63 edifícios com telhado verde ≠ 63 edifícios). Um item pode começar certo e errar só no final. Palavras como only, all e separately costumam decidir.

questoes.enunciado:
Considere os segmentos a seguir.

I - “Its climate is classified as hot semi-arid” (§8) II - “All of the green roofs were of the extensive type and had been installed at least two years before the study began” (§9) III - “seven were drip-irrigated while five relied on rainfall alone” (§9)

Os segmentos sublinhados estão, respectivamente, nos seguintes tempos e vozes verbais:
alternativas: presente simples, voz passiva – passado perfeito, voz passiva – passado simples, voz ativa.
presente simples, voz passiva – passado simples, voz passiva – passado simples, voz ativa.
presente perfeito, voz passiva – passado perfeito, voz ativa – presente simples, voz ativa.
presente simples, voz passiva – presente perfeito, voz passiva – passado simples, voz passiva.
presente simples, voz ativa – passado perfeito, voz passiva – passado simples, voz ativa.
questoes.explicacao:
I: is (presente de be) + particípio classified = presente simples, voz passiva (“é classificado”).

II: had + been + particípio installed = passado perfeito (past perfect), voz passiva (“tinham sido instalados”). Indica uma ação anterior a outra no passado (before the study began). Com has/have been seria presente perfeito.

III: relied = passado simples, voz ativa. O sujeito five (cinco telhados) pratica a ação de “depender”.
questoes.dica: Dica: passiva = forma de be + particípio. O tempo é dado pelo auxiliar: is/are (presente), was/were (passado), has/have been (presente perfeito), had been (passado perfeito), will be (futuro).

questoes.enunciado: O segmento destacado em “so that the green roofs exhibited a consistently pronounced attenuation of the diurnal temperature range” (§12) pode ser traduzido, no contexto em que é empregado, por
alternativas: uma amplitude consistentemente acentuada da atenuação térmica diária.
uma atenuação consistente da acentuada amplitude térmica diária.
uma atenuação consistentemente acentuada da amplitude térmica diária.
uma amplitude térmica diária de atenuação consistente e acentuada.
uma acentuação consistente da atenuação da amplitude térmica diária.
questoes.explicacao:
Divida o sintagma no of:

• a consistently pronounced attenuation: o núcleo é attenuation (atenuação), a última palavra antes do of. pronounced (acentuada, marcante) qualifica o núcleo, e consistently é advérbio (-ly) que modifica pronounced. Fica “uma atenuação consistentemente acentuada”.

• of the diurnal temperature range: núcleo range (amplitude, variação), com temperature e diurnal como modificadores. Fica “da amplitude térmica diária”. Os números confirmam: 9,7 °C sob o substrato contra 38,8 °C nas membranas convencionais.

(a) e (d) põem range como núcleo do sintagma inteiro. (b) liga “acentuada” à amplitude, quando ela modifica a atenuação. (e) cria uma “acentuação” que não existe no original.
questoes.dica: Regra: em inglês, o núcleo é o último substantivo antes do of, e tudo à esquerda o modifica. Traduza do núcleo para a esquerda. Palavras em -ly modificam o adjetivo seguinte, não o substantivo. Um substantivo usado como adjetivo (temperature range) vira locução: “amplitude de temperatura”, ou “térmica”.

questoes.enunciado:
Associe os dados numéricos apresentados nos Resultados (§12–§15) aos seus respectivos referentes. Um dos números não será utilizado.

  1. 27,6 °C
  2. 3,8 °C
  3. 31,2%
  4. 3,1%
  5. 14,5%
  • (  )Diferença entre as temperaturas máximas diárias médias sob substratos de 15 cm e de 8 cm.
  • (  )Redução do consumo de eletricidade para refrigeração no último pavimento dos edifícios com telhado verde.
  • (  )Redução média da maior carga de refrigeração registrada em intervalos de 15 minutos.
  • (  )Diferença de consumo de refrigeração nos pavimentos inferiores, sem significância estatística.

Assinale a sequência correta.
questoes.explicacao:
Roofs with a 15 cm growing medium had a mean daily peak of 31.9 °C, compared with 35.7 °C for those with an 8 cm medium (difference 3.8 °C) (§13) → 2. 27,6 °C é a diferença entre telhados verdes e convencionais (§12), não entre profundidades.

On the uppermost storey, consumption was 31.2% lower (§15) → 3.

Peak cooling demand, defined as the highest 15-minute load …, was on average 14.5% lower (§15) → 5.

on the storeys below the difference was only 3.1% and did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.27) (§15) → 4.

O 27,6 °C (1) fica sem par.
questoes.dica: Dica: para cada número, leia a frase inteira e identifique o que foi comparado (entre grupos? dentro do grupo de telhados verdes? em qual pavimento?). Números parecidos, como 3,1% e 3,8 °C, são postos lado a lado justamente para confundir. Olhe também a unidade (°C × %).

questoes.enunciado: Os segmentos destacados em “a result which is consistent with their suggestion that the benefit increases with incident solar radiation. […] since the latter is exposed to the sun and the former is not, figures obtained by the two methods are not strictly comparable, and the difference between them is likely to account for some part of the discrepancy” (§17) referem-se, respectivamente, a
alternativas: Marlowe and Achterberg – the membrane beneath the growing medium – the vegetated surface itself – figures obtained by the two methods
Marlowe and Achterberg – the vegetated surface itself – the membrane beneath the growing medium – figures obtained by the two methods
temperate summers – the vegetated surface itself – the membrane beneath the growing medium – several earlier studies
Marlowe and Achterberg – the vegetated surface itself – the membrane beneath the growing medium – several earlier studies
several earlier studies – the vegetated surface itself – the sun – figures obtained by the two methods
questoes.explicacao:
their: quem fez a “sugestão” de que o benefício cresce com a radiação solar foi Marlowe and Achterberg (2012), citados na mesma frase (e no §3). Temperate summers não sugerem nada.

the latter / the former: o par está na frase anterior a since: the sensors … were fixed to the membrane beneath the growing medium, whereas several earlier studies measured the temperature of the vegetated surface itself. O último mencionado (latter) é a superfície vegetada, que fica exposta ao sol. O primeiro (former) é a membrana sob o substrato, que não fica. A alternativa (a) inverte os dois.

them: “a diferença entre eles” = entre os números obtidos pelos dois métodos (figures obtained by the two methods), sujeito da oração imediatamente anterior. É essa diferença de método que explica parte da discrepância com os estudos anteriores.
questoes.dica: Dica: com the former / the latter, volte até achar os dois elementos comparados e numere-os na ordem em que aparecem: o primeiro é former, o segundo é latter. Depois, teste pelo sentido (“o que está exposto ao sol?”). Para their/them, procure substantivos no plural que façam sentido com o verbo (suggestion exige quem sugere).

questoes.enunciado: A função do segmento destacado em “Crucially, the saving was confined almost entirely to the uppermost storey, that is, to the zone separated from the green roof by nothing more than the roof slab and a suspended ceiling” (§18) é
alternativas: esclarecer a expressão anterior, especificando o que se entende por ela.
atenuar o grau de comprometimento dos autores em relação ao que é dito.
introduzir um exemplo, entre outros possíveis, do que foi afirmado antes.
introduzir uma conclusão decorrente dos resultados apresentados.
estabelecer contraste com a informação apresentada anteriormente.
questoes.explicacao:
That is (“isto é”, “ou seja”) introduz uma reformulação: the uppermost storey é redito como the zone separated from the green roof by nothing more than the roof slab and a suspended ceiling. A segunda expressão é o mesmo pavimento, descrito de modo a explicar por que a economia se concentra ali.

(c) “Exemplificar” seria for instance / for example / such as: o trecho não dá um exemplo entre vários, dá o mesmo referente com outras palavras. (b) Atenuar seria it is argued, apparently. (d) Concluir seria thus / therefore, como It follows that no fim do parágrafo. (e) Não há oposição.
questoes.dica: Dica: that is, i.e., in other words, namely = esclarecer ou reformular (a mesma coisa dita de outro jeito). for instance, e.g., such as = exemplificar (um caso entre outros). Para distinguir, pergunte: o que vem depois é o mesmo referente ou um caso dele?

questoes.enunciado:
Indique se os segmentos a seguir estão em acordo (A) ou desacordo (D) com o que apresentam os parágrafos 18 a 20.

  • (  )A economia de energia observada ficou acima da relatada por Ostrowska (2018) para escritórios em clima temperado e abaixo da prevista por Quispe-Delgado (2015) para climas áridos.
  • (  )A profundidade do substrato produziu um benefício estável ao longo de toda a estação, ao passo que os telhados não irrigados perderam por completo sua vantagem sobre os convencionais durante a onda de calor.
  • (  )Para os autores, o efeito isolante passivo, embora secundário, está longe de ser desprezível.
  • (  )Os autores estimam que a irrigação por gotejamento com água cinza tratada exigiria volumes modestos de água.

Assinale a sequência correta.
alternativas: A – A – A – D
D – D – A – A
A – D – A – D
A – A – D – A
A – D – D – D
questoes.explicacao:
1 (A): a saving well above the 6 to 9% reported by Ostrowska (2018) for temperate office buildings, yet below the 25% predicted by Quispe-Delgado (2015) for arid climates (§18).

2 (D): a primeira metade está certa (conferred a stable benefit throughout the season), mas os não irrigados perderam much of (grande parte de) sua vantagem, não toda: Non-irrigated roofs nonetheless continued to outperform the conventional roofs throughout the event, albeit by a much narrower margin (§19).

3 (A): the passive insulating effect, though secondary, is far from negligible (§19).

4 (D): a água cinza é apresentada como possibilidade, provided that … the volumes involved prove to be modest, e os autores afirmam que the present study … did not measure water consumption and can offer no estimate of those volumes (§20). “Volumes modestos” é uma condição, não uma estimativa.
questoes.dica: Dica: nos itens de A/D, desconfie de exageros (“por completo”, “sempre”, “todos”) quando o texto usa much of, most, albeit. E não confunda condição (provided that = “desde que”) com afirmação: o que está depois de provided that não foi constatado.

questoes.enunciado: No segmento “Non-irrigated roofs nonetheless continued to outperform the conventional roofs throughout the event, albeit by a much narrower margin” (§19), qual é a relação lógica estabelecida pelo segmento sublinhado?
alternativas: Condição.
Tempo.
Comparação.
Causa.
Concessão.
questoes.explicacao:
Albeit = “embora”, “ainda que”. A ideia principal (os telhados não irrigados continuaram melhores que os convencionais) é mantida apesar de uma ressalva (a margem foi muito menor). É uma concessão.

(c) é a armadilha: há uma comparação em narrower (“mais estreita”), mas quem a faz é o adjetivo comparativo, não o conector sublinhado. (a) Condição seria provided that / if / unless, como no §20. (d) Causa seria since / because. (b) Tempo seria while / when.
questoes.dica: Conectores de concessão: albeit, although, though, even though, despite, in spite of, nonetheless, nevertheless. Note que albeit costuma vir seguido de um adjetivo ou de uma locução, sem verbo (albeit by a narrower margin, albeit slowly).

questoes.enunciado: Assinale a alternativa cujo segmento sublinhado indica alto grau de certeza dos autores em relação ao que afirmam.
alternativas: “[…] the benefit fluctuates with the availability of water and <u>may</u> all but disappear when the substrate dries out” (§2).
“This difference <u>should</u> be interpreted in light of the fact that all buildings were air-conditioned” (§14).
“the owners who chose to install green roofs <u>might</u> differ systematically from those who did not” (§21).
“Where water cannot be supplied during the hottest weeks, the evaporative component of the benefit <u>will</u> be lost” (§24).
“life-cycle assessments <u>could</u> also establish whether the savings reported here justify the costs” (§22).
questoes.explicacao:
Will faz uma afirmação categórica: sem água, a parte evaporativa do benefício “será perdida”. A frase continua com whatever the merits of the planting scheme (“sejam quais forem os méritos do plantio”), o que reforça a certeza.

(a) may e (e) could indicam possibilidade. (c) might é a possibilidade mais fraca, usada para admitir um viés que não pode ser descartado. (b) should indica recomendação (“deve ser interpretada”), não certeza sobre um fato.
questoes.dica: Escala de certeza: might < may / could < should / ought to < will / must / cannot. Lembre que should pode indicar tanto recomendação quanto expectativa provável. Em nenhum dos dois casos é certeza máxima.

questoes.enunciado: Assinale a alternativa que NÃO é apontada pelos autores (§22) como necessidade de futuras pesquisas.
alternativas: Monitorar os mesmos edifícios por vários anos consecutivos, acompanhando o amadurecimento da vegetação e a degradação dos substratos.
Comparar o desempenho de telhados verdes com substratos de diferentes profundidades.
Incluir edifícios residenciais e mais altos, além de edifícios com níveis variados de isolamento da cobertura.
Medir diretamente a água consumida na irrigação e avaliar, no ciclo de vida, se as economias justificam os custos.
Investigar se os telhados verdes têm efeito mensurável sobre a temperatura do ar no nível da rua.
questoes.explicacao:
O §22 pede: (a) Monitoring the same buildings over several consecutive years…; (c) Studies that include residential and taller buildings, as well as buildings with a wider range of roof insulation levels; (d) The water consumed by irrigation should be metered directly … and life-cycle assessments could also establish…; (e) whether the green roofs of Valdoro have any measurable effect on air temperatures at street level remains to be investigated.

(b) é o intruso. A comparação entre substratos de 8 e 15 cm já foi feita neste estudo (pergunta 4, §7; resultados no §13 e na Tabela 1). Não é apresentada como lacuna.
questoes.dica: Dica: em “NÃO é necessidade de pesquisa futura”, o intruso muitas vezes é algo que o próprio estudo já fez. Por ser assunto do texto, parece certo. Confira se cada alternativa está mesmo no parágrafo indicado, e não em Method ou Results.

questoes.enunciado: Qual alternativa sintetiza a CONCLUSÃO (§23–§24) a que chegam os autores do texto?
alternativas: Os telhados verdes são um remédio universal para os problemas térmicos dos edifícios em cidades quentes, e seus benefícios independem das características da construção.
Como a água é escassa em cidades semiáridas, os programas municipais devem abandonar a irrigação e apoiar apenas telhados verdes com substratos profundos.

Os telhados verdes devem ser vistos como uma medida direcionada, cujo valor depende do edifício sob eles e da água disponível, e os incentivos devem priorizar edifícios baixos mal isolados, substratos mais profundos e fontes sustentáveis de irrigação.
Os incentivos municipais devem ser estendidos igualmente a todos os edifícios comerciais, já que os telhados verdes reduziram o consumo de refrigeração em quase um quinto.
Os benefícios dos telhados verdes se distribuíram de forma uniforme entre os pavimentos e foram maiores em edifícios cujas lajes já eram bem isoladas.
questoes.explicacao:
O §24 resume: green roofs should be regarded not as a universal remedy …, but as a targeted measure whose value depends on the building beneath and on the water available above, e os programas deveriam concentrar incentives on poorly insulated low-rise buildings, … favouring deeper growing media …, and … linking support for green roofs to a sustainable source of irrigation water.

(a) contradiz not as a universal remedy. (b) contradiz a proposta de vincular o apoio a uma fonte sustentável de irrigação: não se trata de abandonar a irrigação. (d) contradiz a recomendação de concentrar os incentivos, que é o contrário de rewarding the installation of vegetated roofs as such. (e) contradiz They were concentrated on the top storey (§23) e where the roof slab is already well insulated, much of the remaining benefit will already have been secured by other means (§24).
questoes.dica: Dica: compare cada alternativa com as frases da conclusão. Os distratores costumam contradizer uma frase específica (“universal”, “igualmente”, “uniforme”) ou levar uma recomendação ao extremo (“abandonar”).
